articles.title: Renee Good shooting: Family sues ICE agent, top Trump officials over her death
articles.summary: The family of Renee Good, a 37-year-old mother of three who was fatally shot by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent in Minneapolis in
articles.body: The family of Renee Good, a 37-year-old mother of three who was fatally shot by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent in Minneapolis in January, has filed two civil lawsuits against the US government, the agent, and several Trump administration officials.According to CNN, the lawsuits were filed in Minnesota federal court on Thursday and allege wrongful death, excessive use of force, conspiracy and other violations. One suit names the US government under the Federal Tort Claims Act, while the second names ICE agent Jonathan Ross, several unnamed federal agents and officials including Stephen Miller, Tom Homan and former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem.Good was killed on January 7 during Operation Metro Surge, the Trump administration's immigration enforcement operation in Minneapolis. Her family alleges in the second lawsuit that the operation was a coordinated effort that interfered with the civil rights of people of Somali and Hispanic descent.The lawsuit against the US government seeks unspecified compensation for Good's death and the suffering she allegedly endured before she was killed. It also seeks damages for her partner, Becca Good, who witnessed the shooting, according to the family's attorneys.The second lawsuit accuses Ross and other officials of civil rights violations and alleges that the shooting was the "predictable and intended product" of the immigration operation. The family also alleges that officials failed to properly investigate Good's death.Federal officials have previously said Ross acted in self-defence during the shooting. The Trump administration has rejected the family's allegations. White House spokesperson Lauren Bis said the administration intends to "vigorously defend" the lawsuits, calling them baseless.Good was killed after she and Becca had dropped their 6-year-old son at school and encountered federal immigration officers on a Minneapolis street. Bystander video showed Good inside a red SUV as officers ordered her to get out of the vehicle before Ross opened fire.An analysis of video footage by AP and others found that Ross fired into the vehicle as it turned away from him, according to the news agency. Federal officials had said at the time that the agent acted in self-defence.Speaking at a news conference announcing the lawsuits, Becca Good said Renee was "the love of my life" and described the impact of her death on their children. She said the family was seeking accountability and changes to prevent another family from experiencing a similar loss.The lawsuits came months after Good's death sparked protests and renewed scrutiny of the Trump administration's immigration enforcement operations in Minneapolis. articles.title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay’s ‘chai pe charcha’ during bypoll campaign trail
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister and Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) founder C Joseph Vijay stopped at a tea shop during his roadshow in Madurantakam
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister and Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) founder C Joseph Vijay stopped at a tea shop during his roadshow in Madurantakam on Friday, interacted with people and had tea with them, as he campaigned for his party’s candidate ahead of the October 6 bypoll.A video shared by news agency PTI showed Vijay stepping out of his campaign vehicle and stopping at the tea shop. He was seen interacting with people gathered there and having tea with them.The chief minister was in Madurantakam to seek votes for TVK nominee Maragatham Kumaravel, who is contesting the bypoll to the Assembly constituency. Vijay’s campaign also saw him drive a tractor through agricultural fields during his visit to a village near the town.Vijay drives tractor during campaignVijay’s motorcade came to a halt near a village when he spotted a farmer operating a tractor by the roadside. The chief minister, dressed in a white shirt and dhoti, got down from his campaign vehicle and walked towards the fields to speak to the farmer, who welcomed him.Vijay then took the driver’s seat and drove the tractor across the slushy fields for a few minutes. He later brought it out onto the main road, where people waiting nearby greeted him.Vijay is known for driving vehicles at official events. His decision to drive a tractor came amid his campaign for the October 6 bypolls.Vijay covers over 30 villages in roadshowThe TVK chief held a roadshow across Madurantakam, covering more than 30 villages and a cluster of neighbourhoods in the Assembly constituency, around 100 km from Chennai.People gathered outside their homes and along roads in villages and semi-urban neighbourhoods to catch a glimpse of Vijay. He waved at them, greeted them with folded hands and sought votes for the party.TVK workers also organised cultural programmes and dance performances at town squares for people waiting to see the chief minister.Bypolls in Madurantakam, Dharapuram on October 6The bypolls in Madurantakam and Dharapuram were necessitated after legislators Maragatham Kumaravel and P Sathyabama resigned from their Assembly seats and quit the AIADMK. Both subsequently joined the ruling TVK and have been renominated from their respective constituencies.Opposition parties have accused the ruling party of horse-trading, making it a key issue in the bypoll campaign.Polling for both constituencies will be held on October 6.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
